Plan Your Trip
Ways to travel

Three things, done properly

I've narrowed what I plan to cruises, all-inclusive resorts, and small group tours — plus the honeymoons and LGBTQ+ travel that sit on top of them.

Plenty of advisors will book you anything. In practice that means broad familiarity and deep knowledge of almost nothing — which is fine right up until the moment it matters, which is usually the moment you're choosing between two cabins or two room categories and nobody can tell you the difference.

So I stopped. These three are what I know properly: I've sailed the ships, walked the resorts, and know which tour operators enforce their group caps. Everything below is organised by how you travel rather than where, because in my experience that's the decision that actually determines whether you enjoy the trip.

Cruises

Ocean, river, and expedition. CLIA Certified Cruise Counsellor, with line certifications across Virgin Voyages, Royal Caribbean, and Carnival.

Plan a cruise

All-Inclusive Resorts

Certified with Sandals and the Hyatt Inclusive Collection. The room category matters more than the resort, and almost nobody tells you that.

Find a resort

Small Group Tours

Real group caps, employed guides, and honest inclusion lists. For the places where going independently is more work than it's worth.

Browse tours

Honeymoons & Romance

Built on the same three foundations, with the upgrades and celebration perks requested properly — which is the only way they actually arrive.

Plan a honeymoon

LGBTQ+ Travel

NGLCC-certified. Which ships, resorts, and destinations are genuinely welcoming — and which ones just have a rainbow on the landing page in June.

Travel with confidence

What if I want something else?

Ask. Plenty of trips are adjacent — a land package either side of a sailing, a family celebration that needs eight rooms, a rail journey. If it's close to what I do well, I'll take it on. If it isn't, I'll tell you straight rather than take the booking and learn on your holiday. That's a better outcome for both of us.
